summary: SANS Internet Storm Center published its daily cybersecurity briefing covering current threat landscape developments and security intelligence. The podcast format provides analysis of emerging security incidents and vulnerabilities affecting the threat environment.

title: Rockwell Automation FactoryTalk Historian Site Edition Vulnerabilities
summary: CISA disclosed three vulnerabilities in Rockwell Automation FactoryTalk Historian Site Edition affecting version 11 and earlier. These issues enable authentication bypass through repeated login requests, denial-of-service conditions via uncaught exceptions, and potential data loss in snapshot caches. Rockwell Automation provides patches and recommends network segmentation, service monitoring, and access controls for affected deployments.

title: AryStinger botnet compromises thousands of D-Link routers globally
summary: A previously undocumented botnet named AryStinger has infected over 4,000 D-Link routers, primarily targeting older models. The compromised devices are being repurposed as proxies for routing malicious traffic. This campaign demonstrates continued vulnerability exploitation in legacy networking hardware.

title: OXLOADER Malware Loader Distributes CastleStealer via Malicious Google Ads
summary: Researchers at Elastic Security Labs identified a new campaign using a previously unknown loader called OXLOADER to deliver CastleStealer malware. The distribution mechanism exploits malicious Google Ads to initiate infection, with attribution indicators suggesting Russian-speaking threat actors motivated by financial gain.

title: Addressing Security Debt Through Exposure Management
summary: Security teams can reduce technical debt by focusing on two core questions: identifying which vulnerabilities are externally exposed and establishing acceptable remediation timelines. This exposure-centric approach prioritizes risk based on actual attack surface rather than vulnerability inventory size.

title: eBanking Phishing Campaign Using IPv4-Mapped IPv6 Addresses
summary: A phishing campaign targeting a major Belgian financial institution was observed using IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses to deliver malicious content. This obfuscation technique may allow threat actors to evade traditional network filtering rules that focus on IPv4-based detection patterns.

title: AI Agents as Unmanaged Identities Create Enterprise Governance Gap
summary: AI agents increasingly function as autonomous identities within enterprise environments, accessing data and executing critical workflows, yet most organizations lack adequate oversight mechanisms. Security researchers highlight that treating AI agents as managed identities—similar to user and service account governance—is essential to mitigate unauthorized system interactions and access.

title: Google Enforces Android Developer Verification in Four Countries Starting September 2026
summary: Google will require Android developers to complete identity verification starting September 30, 2026, in Brazil, Indonesia, Singapore, and Thailand. Unverified apps will be blocked from installation on certified Android devices in these regions. Major device manufacturers have committed to implementing this requirement from launch.

title: WhatsApp Phishing Campaign Distributes VBScript Malware
summary: A malware campaign targets WhatsApp users across multiple countries using fraudulent business documents to deliver VBScript files that grant attackers remote access to compromised systems. The attack leverages social engineering through the messaging platform to bypass traditional email-based defenses.

title: WhatsApp VBScript Campaign Distributes ManageEngine RMM Tool via Malicious Documents
summary: A multi-region campaign is delivering malicious VBScript files through WhatsApp direct messages, disguised as legitimate documents, to facilitate unauthorized installation of ManageEngine RMM software. The threat targets WhatsApp Desktop and Web users across multiple countries including Malaysia, Brazil, India, Mexico, Singapore, the UK, Spain, Taiwan, and Australia. Kaspersky researchers identified the campaign as actively distributing the payload to gain remote access capabilities on compromised systems.

title: CVE-2024-40766: Patching Insufficient Without Configuration Remediation
summary: A vulnerability tracked as CVE-2024-40766 has been addressed through patching, yet organizations deploying the fix may remain exposed if underlying configuration issues are not separately remediated. The case illustrates a common gap where technical patches alone do not eliminate risk when misconfigurations persist in affected systems.

title: JaredFromSubway MEV Bot Compromised in $15M Cryptocurrency Theft
summary: An attacker exploited vulnerabilities in the JaredFromSubway Ethereum MEV bot by fabricating false trading opportunities, resulting in a $15 million loss. The incident highlights operational risks within automated cryptocurrency trading infrastructure where logic-layer vulnerabilities can be leveraged for financial theft.

title: OpenAI Releases GPT-5.5-Cyber Model for Vulnerability Detection and Remediation
summary: OpenAI has expanded its Daybreak initiative by releasing an improved GPT-5.5-Cyber model to trusted security defenders. The model is designed to identify software vulnerabilities and support patching efforts, with enhanced capability to perform sustained analysis across large codebases.

title: ISC Stormcast For Tuesday, June 23rd, 2026
summary: SANS Internet Storm Center's daily podcast briefing covering current cybersecurity developments and threat landscape updates. The episode provides analysis of recent security incidents and emerging threat patterns relevant to security practitioners.

title: FFmpeg PixelSmash vulnerability enables remote code execution and denial of service
summary: A vulnerability in FFmpeg's video decoder, designated PixelSmash, permits remote code execution on Jellyfin servers and denial-of-service attacks against multiple media and content management applications including Kodi, Emby, Nextcloud, PhotoPrism, and OBS Studio. The flaw affects widely deployed open-source software across media streaming and collaborative platforms.

title: FortiBleed Campaign Exploits FortiGate Devices with Custom Credential Harvesting Tools
summary: SOCRadar researchers identified a large-scale campaign targeting Fortinet FortiGate firewalls that deployed custom packet sniffers to extract authentication credentials from compromised devices. The campaign, termed FortiBleed, represents a credential theft operation leveraging vulnerabilities or misconfigurations in widely deployed network security appliances.

title: Legacy Infrastructure Vulnerabilities Enable AI Agent Hijacking
summary: Security leaders face an emerging gap where attackers exploit outdated infrastructure to compromise AI agents, taking advantage of the speed of AI adoption outpacing security program maturity. Organizations deploying AI agents without addressing legacy system weaknesses create pathways for threat actors to circumvent AI-specific security controls.

title: Microsoft announces Windows 11 26H2 feature update with streamlined upgrade path
summary: Microsoft has confirmed Windows 11 version 26H2 as the next feature update, with devices currently running 24H2 or 25H2 able to upgrade via a lightweight enablement package rather than a full installation. This approach continues Microsoft's shift toward smaller, more frequent updates.

title: Weekly Threat Recap: Browser Vulnerabilities, EDR Evasion, Botnet Activity, and Mobile Malware
summary: Weekly threat landscape includes browser vulnerabilities, tools designed to disable endpoint detection and response solutions, television-based botnet infrastructure, OpenBSD security flaws, and Android trojans with excessive permissions. Recurring attack patterns involve credential compromise, malicious software distribution, browser extensions with broad access, and WordPress site exploitation.

title: Canada's CSIS Obtains First Threat Reduction Warrant to Remediate Botnet Infections
summary: Canada's Security Intelligence Service (CSIS) obtained judicial authorization to directly remediate botnet malware on infected Canadian infrastructure, including servers, routers, and IoT devices operated by foreign threat actors. The Federal Court warrant, publicly disclosed in June, represents the first operational use of CSIS's threat reduction powers for this purpose.

title: AryStinger Malware Leverages Legacy Routers for Reconnaissance Infrastructure
summary: Security researchers identified AryStinger, a malware family targeting legacy home routers to establish a distributed reconnaissance and proxy network. The campaign has compromised at least 4,300 routers, with infections continuing to increase. Unlike traditional router botnets used for DDoS attacks, AryStinger focuses on reconnaissance activities that precede actual system compromise.

title: INTERPOL Reports Rising Cybercrime Threats in Asia-Pacific Region
summary: INTERPOL's 2025/2026 assessment identifies significant growth in cybercrime across Asia and the South Pacific, driven by rapid digital adoption and varying cybersecurity capabilities. The report highlights phishing as the most prevalent threat, alongside ransomware and AI-enabled scams, exacerbated by organized criminal networks exploiting regional security disparities.

title: 2026 Breach Impact Study
summary: Verizon and CyberAcuView released the inaugural Breach Impact Study, analyzing approximately 70,000 cyber insurance claims (38,000 with recorded payouts) covering insurable incidents from January 2019 through October 2025 in the United States. The study addresses a frequently requested question about financial impact quantification by examining ground-up losses—combining deductibles and incurred losses—across multiple loss types including ransomware and business email compromise claims. The dataset represents insurable loss only, functioning as a conservative lower bound of actual economic impact, as it excludes uninsured losses, reputational damage, and non-claim costs, with additional limitations from policy sublimits and insurance tower structures. The report segments findings by incident type, industry sector (including healthcare, manufacturing, retail, and small/medium-sized businesses), and organizational size, utilizing statistical rigor and uncertainty visualization consistent with the Data Breach Investigations Report methodology.

title: Scattered Spider Members Plead Guilty in Transport for London Attack
summary: Two individuals affiliated with the Scattered Spider cybercrime group entered guilty pleas in UK court regarding an August 2024 attack on Transport for London that disrupted regional public transit operations. The guilty pleas on trial's opening day concluded what was anticipated to be a lengthy judicial proceeding.

title: Cisco Unified Communications Manager SSRF vulnerability CVE-2026-20230 under active exploitation
summary: A high-severity server-side request forgery (SSRF) vulnerability in Cisco Unified Communications Manager has transitioned from disclosure to active exploitation in the wild. The flaw allows attackers to bypass network controls and access internal resources through the affected communications platform.

title: Cisco Unified CM Vulnerability Under Active Exploitation Following PoC Release
summary: A critical flaw in Cisco Unified Communications Manager and Unified CM Session Management Edition (CVE-2026-20230, CVSS 8.6) is being actively exploited in the wild following public disclosure of proof-of-concept code. The vulnerability stems from improper input validation in HTTP request handling, permitting unauthenticated remote attackers to achieve file-write capabilities and potential privilege escalation to root.

title: Salesforce Customer Data Exposed Through Compromised Klue OAuth Tokens
summary: Attackers who breached application vendor Klue leveraged stolen OAuth tokens to access and exfiltrate Salesforce data from multiple customers. The scope of affected organizations continues to expand as additional victims are identified in connection with the Icarus threat actor's campaign.

title: Tata Electronics Confirms Cyberattack with Data Breach
summary: Tata Electronics acknowledged a cyberattack affecting portions of its IT infrastructure, with threat actors subsequently releasing stolen data. The company has confirmed the incident but detailed information regarding the scope and nature of compromised systems remains limited.

title: FortiBleed Campaign Targets 430,000+ FortiGate Firewalls in Credential Harvesting Operation
summary: A Russian-speaking financially-motivated initial access broker has conducted a large-scale credential harvesting campaign against over 430,000 FortiGate firewalls worldwide since February 2026. The operation involves credential collection, service enumeration, brute-force attacks, and deployment of custom malware to establish initial access for downstream exploitation.

title: Cordyceps Campaign: Malicious Pull Requests Target Developer CI/CD Workflows
summary: A coordinated campaign dubbed 'Cordyceps' has exploited CI/CD pipeline vulnerabilities across multiple high-profile open-source projects, including Microsoft Azure Sentinel, Google's AI Agent Development Kit, Apache Doris, Cloudflare Workers SDK, and Python's Black formatter. The attack leverages compromised pull requests to inject malicious code into developer workflows, demonstrating continued targeting of supply chain infrastructure.

title: ISC Stormcast - Wednesday, June 24th, 2026
summary: SANS Internet Storm Center's daily podcast briefing covering current cybersecurity developments and threat landscape updates for practitioners and security professionals.

title: Windows 11 KB5095093 introduces Point-in-Time restore capability
summary: Microsoft has released preview cumulative update KB5095093 for Windows 11 versions 24H2 and 25H2, addressing multiple bugs and introducing a new Point-in-Time restore feature. This functionality allows users to revert systems to previous states without full system recovery procedures.

title: Fake AI Agent Skill Bypassed Security Scanners and Reached 26,000 Deployments
summary: Security firm AIR demonstrated a vulnerability in AI agent skill marketplaces by deploying a benign test skill that circumvented all security scanners it encountered and was installed across approximately 26,000 agents, including those in corporate environments. The proof-of-concept collected user email addresses while evading detection, highlighting gaps in skill validation mechanisms across marketplace platforms.

title: SocGholish Takedown Highlights Malicious TDS Threats
summary: Law enforcement action against SocGholish has demonstrated how traffic distribution systems serve as initial access brokers for major cybercriminal groups, including Evil Corp. TDS infrastructure enables attackers to selectively route compromised traffic toward different payloads and exploit chains, creating a layered attack surface that complicates detection and response.

title: Healthtech firm Xsolis suffers data breach impacting 1.4 million people
summary: Healthcare technology company Xsolis disclosed a data breach affecting approximately 1.4 million individuals. The incident resulted from a successful phishing campaign that granted attackers network access and exposed sensitive personal data.

title: Trump Executive Order Establishes 2030-2031 Timeline for Federal Post-Quantum Cryptography Migration
summary: An executive order signed on June 22 mandates that U.S. federal agencies transition high-value assets and critical systems to post-quantum cryptographic standards by specified deadlines: key establishment by end of 2030 and digital signatures by end of 2031. National security systems operate under separate migration parameters. The directive reflects ongoing concerns about quantum computing threats to current encryption infrastructure.

title: FortiBleed: Attackers Deploy Credential-Stealing Tool Against FortiGate Firewalls
summary: Threat actors have developed a Golang-based packet sniffer to target approximately 430,000 FortiGate firewalls globally, successfully extracting roughly 110 million credentials. The tool exploits compromised firewalls to intercept and harvest authentication data, representing an ongoing large-scale campaign affecting organizations worldwide.

title: White House Executive Order on Post-Quantum Cryptography Transition
summary: The U.S. Presidential Executive Order issued June 22, 2026, mandates a coordinated federal migration to NIST-approved post-quantum cryptography (PQC) standards to counter threats from future quantum computing capabilities and current harvest-now-decrypt-later attacks. Federal agencies must designate PQC migration leads within 30 days and transition high-value assets and high-impact systems to PQC-based key establishment by December 31, 2030, and digital signatures by December 31, 2031. OMB, NIST, NSA, and CISA are tasked with providing technical guidance, with NIST conducting a PQC pilot by end of 2027. Sector Risk Management Agencies must assist critical infrastructure operators in developing migration plans, while the State Department coordinates international adoption of NIST PQC standards. The order also requires development of cryptographic bills of materials and cost optimization strategies across federal procurement.

title: CISA alerts to active exploitation of critical Ubiquiti and Lantronix vulnerabilities
summary: CISA has issued a warning regarding adversaries actively exploiting maximum-severity vulnerabilities in Ubiquiti UniFi OS and Lantronix serial-to-ethernet server products. The agency is tracking in-the-wild exploitation of these flaws, indicating immediate risk to organizations operating affected infrastructure.

title: CISA Alerts on Active Exploitation of Critical Lantronix EDS5000 Vulnerability
summary: CISA has issued a warning regarding CVE-2025-67038, a critical code injection flaw (CVSS 9.8) in Lantronix EDS5000 Series devices that is currently being exploited in the wild. Federal agencies have been directed to remediate the vulnerability by June 26, 2026.

title: Malicious OpenClaw Packages Bypass Security Checks in AI Skills Marketplace
summary: OpenClaw removed five packages from its ClawHub skills marketplace that contained infostealers and other malware despite passing security validation. The incident highlights vulnerabilities in the AI supply chain where malicious code can evade detection mechanisms in third-party package repositories.

title: Siemens SINEC INS Multiple Vulnerabilities Disclosed
summary: Siemens SINEC INS versions prior to V1.0 SP2 Update 6 contain four vulnerabilities including OS command injection, path traversal, privilege escalation via unnecessary capabilities, and weak password hashing with static salt. The vulnerabilities affect critical infrastructure sectors worldwide and require immediate patching to V1.0 SP2 Update 6 or later.

title: Microsoft and Europol Disrupt Amadey and StealC Malware Operations
summary: Microsoft, Europol, and international law enforcement partners have dismantled infrastructure supporting the Amadey and StealC malware campaigns under Operation Endgame. The coordinated action targeted command-and-control systems used by these cybercriminal operations, which distribute information-stealing malware and support ransomware activities.

title: Amadey and StealC Malware Network Disrupted, 27M Stolen Credentials Recovered
summary: Law enforcement and private sector partners including Bitdefender, Bitsight, ESET, and Microsoft have dismantled criminal infrastructure associated with Amadey and StealC malware variants. The operation recovered approximately 27 million stolen credentials and targeted the distribution chains used to facilitate ransomware deployments, financial fraud, and attacks against critical infrastructure.

title: macOS Vulnerability Allows Non-Privileged Security Tool Disablement
summary: A macOS flaw enables attackers to disable security and browser protection features without requiring administrator credentials or kernel-level exploits. The vulnerability reduces the attack surface needed for compromise, as adversaries can leverage standard user access to circumvent built-in protections.

title: Service Desk Social Engineering: Attack Vectors and Defense Strategies
summary: Service desks remain high-value targets for social engineers attempting to obtain password resets, modify MFA settings, and gain unauthorized account access. Organizations can reduce susceptibility through verification protocols, staff training, and access controls that limit service desk personnel privileges.

title: DifyTap Vulnerabilities Enable Unauthorized Access to AI Chat Histories
summary: Four vulnerabilities in Dify, an AI application development platform, allow attackers to access and exfiltrate sensitive chat data without detection. The flaws enable unauthorized retrieval of conversation histories stored within deployments using the platform.

title: Mistic backdoor linked to KongTuke ransomware access broker
summary: A previously undocumented backdoor named Mistic has been deployed in financially motivated campaigns against organizations across insurance, education, IT, and professional services sectors. The malware has been attributed to KongTuke, a known ransomware access broker, indicating potential precursor activity for downstream encryption attacks.

title: Evolution Toward Machine-Speed Threat Landscapes
summary: Cybersecurity operations are transitioning from human-paced threat cycles to accelerated threat environments where traditional patching timelines become less viable. The established vulnerability disclosure and remediation workflow—spanning weeks or months from discovery to deployment—faces pressure from faster-moving attack patterns, potentially extending organizational dwell times.

title: SIM Swap Attacks Enable Interception of SMS-Based One-Time Passwords
summary: SIM swap attacks allow threat actors to intercept one-time passwords delivered via SMS, enabling account takeovers despite users believing their accounts are protected. Security practitioners should implement layered authentication mechanisms beyond SMS-based OTP delivery, such as app-based authenticators or hardware security keys.

title: macOS ClickFix Campaign Deploys Infostealer via DMG Mounting
summary: A new macOS-targeted ClickFix campaign leverages Terminal commands to silently download and mount malicious disk images that execute infostealer malware. The attack chain abstracts user interaction by automating DMG mounting and execution steps, reducing visibility into the infection process.

title: DoJ Seizes Huione Cloud Account Connected to Cyber Scam Money Laundering Operations
summary: The U.S. Department of Justice announced the seizure of a cloud computing account operated by subsidiaries of Cambodia-based Huione Group, allegedly used to facilitate money laundering for cyber scam proceeds. Concurrently, the Treasury Department imposed sanctions on nine individuals and 26 entities affiliated with Prince Group in connection with similar illicit financial activities.

title: Scattered Spider members plead guilty to Transport for London hack
summary: Two members of the Scattered Spider cybercriminal group entered guilty pleas for their involvement in the 2024 compromise of Transport for London systems. The case represents judicial action against actors from a group known for targeting critical infrastructure and financial institutions.

title: GitHub Updates actions/checkout to Block Pwn Request Attack Patterns
summary: GitHub is implementing protections in the actions/checkout action to prevent pwn request attacks that leverage pull_request_target workflow triggers to execute malicious code with elevated privileges. The update takes effect June 18, 2026, strengthening supply chain security by mitigating a known exploitation vector in CI/CD pipelines.

title: Passwordless Authentication as Structural Enterprise Requirement in 2026
summary: Passwordless authentication using FIDO2 and passkeys has transitioned from emerging practice to mandatory requirement for enterprise identity security, driven by phishing-resistance demands, regulatory pressure (NIST AM2/AM3, EIDAS), and zero-trust architecture evolution. The critical vulnerability in current deployments is insecure recovery and enrollment flows; attackers now target helpdesk processes rather than passwords directly, with recent breaches at MGM Resorts and Marks & Spencer exploiting weak recovery mechanisms. Effective governance requires four pillars: identity environment verification, device binding via hardware-backed storage (TPM, Secure Enclave), lifecycle management across managed and personal devices, and hardened recovery using verified device rebinding, identity proofing, or policy-controlled helpdesk flows with audit traces. Modern solutions integrate continuous authentication through device posture assessment, contextual risk engines evaluating geovelocity and IP reputation, and emerging Shared Signals Framework for cross-tool risk sharing. Implementation challenges center on legacy systems (Radius, VPN, VDI, mainframes) lacking FIDO2 protocol support; recommended approach prioritizes SaaS and managed endpoints first, applying equivalent-security alternatives for legacy gaps rather than password reversion.
